 Dengue risk high in 29 DSCC wards
 28 wards at moderate risk, 18 at low risk: survey 
 Published : 5 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 5 November 2026, 08:50
 • 
 BANGLADESH
 SHARE 
 Staff Correspondent 
 Aedes larvae, pupae found in 403 households 
 Survey covers 2,250 households across 75 wards 
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 Buckets, drums among major breeding sites 
 Special mosquito-control drives under way 
 Residents urged to remove stagnant water weekly 
 Twenty-nine of the 75 wards under Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) have been identified as high-risk areas for dengue transmission, while 28 are at moderate risk and 18 at low risk, according to a survey.
 The findings were announced yesterday by DSCC Administrator Abdus Salam at a programme at Nagar Bhaban in the capital.
 The survey, conducted by a 36-member DSCC team from September 27 to October 8, covered 2,250 households, with 30 selected from each ward.
 Aedes mosquito larvae and pupae were found in 403 households, according to the findings presented by DSCC Chief Health Officer Dr Jahane Ferdous Binte Rahman.
 The survey identified multi-storey buildings (31.06 percent), standalone houses (31.37 percent), semi-pucca houses (17.39 percent), buildings under construction (13.4 percent) and vacant plots (14.21 percent) as breeding sites.
 The findings showed that plastic buckets accounted for 14.21 percent of larval breeding sites, followed by plastic drums (11.22 percent), stagnant water in basements (9.98 percent), plastic mugs (9.23 percent) and flower pots (5.99 percent).
 The survey also found that nearly half (50.9 percent) of Aedes mosquito breeding and dengue transmission could be prevented at an early stage if residents remained vigilant about their courtyards and water-holding containers.
 Speaking at the event, Abdus Salam urged residents to keep their homes and workplaces clean and remove stagnant water at least once a week, saying government efforts alone would not be enough to prevent dengue.
 He said special mosquito-control drives and awareness programmes were continuing in high-risk areas based on the findings.
 DSCC has also launched an initiative to clean courtyards and toilets at all primary schools during its regular Saturday “Cleaning Day” programme to protect children from dengue, he added.
 “Through public awareness and coordinated efforts, we can build a dengue-free, safe and healthy Dhaka,” he said.
 The survey findings were analysed using the Breteau Index, House Index, Container Index and Pupal Index to identify dengue hotspots.
 DSCC has divided the wards in three categories based on the density of mosquito larvae:
 High-risk (29 wards): 1, 2, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 19, 20, 21, 22, 24, 25, 26, 27, 31, 53, 54, 55, 56, 58, 59, 60, 61, 62, 65 and 71.
 Moderate-risk (28 wards): 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 18, 23, 29, 30, 32, 33, 35, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 43, 46, 51, 52, 57, 64, 67, 68, 69, 73 and 75.
 For all latest news, follow The Daily Star's Google News channel. 
 Low-risk (18 wards): 3, 7, 17, 28, 34, 41, 42, 44, 45, 47, 48, 49, 50, 63, 66, 70, 72 and 74.
